Use the supplied sketch ONLY for the string arrangement and central grip location. The bow FRAME SHAPE may be freely redesigned into an elegant original futuristic weapon; do not mechanically trace the crude angular outline. Ignore the handwritten label and arrow as artwork.

ESSENTIAL STRING TOPOLOGY:
There is ONE MAIN SHOOTING STRING on the far RIGHT, a straight taut vertical line from the upper bowtip to the lower bowtip, in UNDRAWN state.
Inside the main open bow belly, FOUR LONG PARALLEL MUSICAL STRINGS run vertically, DIRECTLY FROM THE UPPER BOW LIMB TO THE LOWER BOW LIMB. Each musical string passes through the horizontal height of the grip, with substantial length BOTH ABOVE AND BELOW the grip. Their lower ends attach directly to separate anchor studs distributed down the curving LOWER BOW LIMB, well BELOW the hand grip. Their upper ends attach directly to the upper bow limb. Lengths progressively increase toward the right main bowstring, as shown in the sketch.
All FOUR long musical strings must visibly connect upper limb to lower limb, making almost the entire bow interior a harp. This is NOT a small harp sitting above a grip: NO little harp insert, NO crossbar or bottom bridge above the grip, NO half-height harp, NO musical strings ending near the handgrip. The only musical-string lower anchors are on the LOWER curved limb. Straight musical strings, not sagging; slightly luminous pale blue, distinct from the single primary string.
The wrapped GRIP sits in the LEFT frame at EXACTLY the SAME HEIGHT AS THE MIDPOINT OF THE MAIN STRING. The right-angle line between grip center and main-string midpoint would be horizontal, but do not draw a guide. Keep the actual handgrip at the full weapon's vertical center. Leave open finger clearance between the grip and leftmost musical string, no strings passing through the grip.
